title: SK Hynix Sees AI Memory Shortage Persisting Through 2030

tickers.name: SK hynix Inc. American Depositary Shares

summary:
The South Korean chipmaker announced that its production capacity for high-bandwidth memory and DRAM is already effectively exhausted for the next several years, with the majority of its volumes through 2029 committed to customers. To support shareholders following a recent decline in its stock price, SK Hynix declared it would distribute at least 50% of its cumulative free cash flow between 2025 and 2027, which includes $75B in dividends and buybacks for the 2026 calendar year.

The outlook that the global memory shortage will likely persist through 2030 comes as the firm reported quarterly revenue of $78.9B and operating profit of $62.8B, both of which beat market estimates. These results and the projection of long-term demand contrast with fears of a 2027 oversupply that have weighed on memory stocks recently, though Dell CEO Michael Dell warned that the current chip crunch could worsen in the short term as he manages a $95B backlog of AI servers.

Jensen Huang just pushed back HARD on the memory oversupply fears.

Speaking to CNBC at GTC Berlin, the $NVDA CEO said he does not see a surplus of memory by 2029, even after the selloff in memory stocks this past week.

"One of the things that's really great about memory is that you can always use more of it," he said.

He added that HBM will be used for years to come, and pointed out that Nvidia was the first company to bring LPDDR into the data center.

The selloff started after a Korean newspaper column predicted a memory price war by 2029, and it dragged down $MU, Samsung and SK Hynix.

When the biggest buyer of AI memory on the planet tells you demand keeps growing, I would take that more seriously than an opinion column.
